title: Basic operations and coefficient reduction
statement:
For the derived-complete
coefficient categories, reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$ commutes
with derived pullback, tensor, ordinary direct image and compact-support
direct image on their stated bounded domains. Finite reduction
$A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ commutes with pullback, tensor and
compact-support direct image on the finite-Tor domains.
For $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, internal Hom and evaluation commute
with reduction for arbitrary first variables on the stated integral
domains. Between finite quotient rings, the elementary comparison
proved here assumes that the first variable is
site-perfect; this includes
the coefficient dual of a perfect complex at a point.
For admissible
exceptional adjoints, use the coefficient comparisons required in
that admissibility hypothesis. The same operations and comparisons
commute with rationalization
and common-stage
scalar extension. All the displayed comparisons preserve the tensor
associativity maps, evaluations, units and counits used to construct
the projection and exchange transformations.

proof.text: For finite ring changes use ringed derived monoidality. For completed pullback and tensor use integral preservation, then the strict coherence and substitution theorems: the specified associators and units are limits of the coefficient tensor maps, not identities inferred from individual reductions.

Apply perfect-source scalar Hom to finite quotients, with arbitrary second variable; perfect duality also makes the point dual perfect. Apply the ambient integral Hom theorem on its stated integral domains, without imposing perfectness on the first variable. All these maps are evaluation transposes.

The direct-image constructibility theorem gives its canonical reduction isomorphism and uniform bound. The DVR theorem makes the coefficient ring Noetherian; standard perfect quotients and the projection map identify this with ordinary completed-ring direct image through the strict derived-limit theorem.

Apply the completed compactification realization to the chosen proper/open factorization. It supplies the actual strict-tower identification and projection normalization on the bounded constructible domain. Between finite quotients use finite compact-support coefficient change on its finite-Tor domain.

For finite field extensions, finite-free completed scalar comparison verifies the hypotheses for direct-image coherence and arbitrary-variable scalar Hom. Integral pullback/tensor scalar comparison and normalized open tensor give the other comparisons. Scalar-completion associator normalization for the explicit rho-coefficient maps and termwise product-cone functors transports their identity and tower equations to the prescribed scalar functors; internal-Hom comparison composition fixes the successive Hom maps. The two open tower routes restrict to the identity and agree by full faithfulness. Step 4 then identifies the proper/open composite with defined compact support.

The mate counit and unit equations, applied to these tensor-coherent comparisons, give the specified projection and exchange squares. The compactification lemma fixes the completed compact-support projection realization. Exceptional comparisons are used only with the isomorphism requirements of admissibility. No invertibility is inferred merely from taking a mate.

source.place: all paragraphs and original steps 7 and 10

proof.text: Rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] is raw localization at $\varpi_E$. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to the exact integral functors and comparisons of steps 1-6, with $\phi=\mathrm{id}$, and $\phi:\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_L$ for scalar comparisons: they extend uniquely, inverses stay inverses, and unit, associator, counit and square equations persist. The transitions of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] are exact [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated], composed by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], the rationalized integral composition maps of step 5's tower laws. Each finite diagram lives over one field and equality is detected after enlargement, so the equations hold there.
